samples.summary: New `.catch(() => {})` plus `fonts.check()`'s fallback semantics make the font guard pass vacuously when the webfont stylesheet never loads
samples.evidence: The load pass now swallows every rejection (`document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})`, line 374). The comment claims "the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family", and docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-55 repeats that "an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com now reports a clear timeout". Per CSS Font Loading, `document.fonts.check()` returns true when no matching FontFace is registered (the text would render with a fallback), so if index.html's Google Fonts stylesheet fails or is blocked (offline/sandboxed CI), zero Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains faces are registered, every `check(...)` at line 388 returns true immediately, and the follow-up loading poll (line 395) also passes because no face is in `loading`. The harness then screenshots the fallback-serif rendering — precisely the failure this change exists to catch. Before the diff, a rejected `fonts.load()` would have propagated out of `page.evaluate` and failed the run loudly; that detection is now removed. A real assertion would require the family to be present, e.g. checking `[...document.fonts].some(f => f.family === family && f.status === 'loaded')`.

samples.summary: Catch-all "no FontFace in status: loading" poll is trivially satisfiable and adds essentially no coverage
samples.evidence: Line 394-398 polls `[...document.fonts].every((face) => face.status !== "loading")`. FontFace status is `unloaded` before a fetch starts and `error` on failure, so the predicate is true both when nothing has begun loading and when every fetch has already failed. The comment at lines 336-338 sells this as a catch-all for "families nobody thought to list here", but a face that is needed and not yet requested reads as `unloaded` and passes on the first poll iteration, so the guard cannot fail in the scenario it is advertised to cover.

samples.summary: Several entries of the new weight matrix assert nothing because those weights are never served
samples.evidence: VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS = [400, 500, 600, 700] is applied to every family, but packages/frontend/index.html:12 requests `Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,500;600;700` (no 400) and `JetBrains Mono:wght@400;500` (no 600/700). CSS font matching resolves those requests to the nearest available face, so `check("400 12px \"Fraunces\"")` and `check("700 12px \"JetBrains Mono\"")` re-assert a face already covered by another weight rather than adding coverage — the matrix is broader than the real face set and gives a false impression of per-weight verification.

samples.summary: No test or assertion verifies the fixed behavior (fonts actually applied at capture time); the only coverage is the same pixel baselines the bug already slipped past
samples.evidence: The change fixes a capture-time race whose sole failure signal is the visual baseline diff that already produced a false-negative-then-flake on PR #770 (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:5-18). Nothing added asserts, e.g., that a preview element's used font family is Inter rather than the fallback serif before the screenshot, so a future regression in waitForFontsReady is again only detectable as a flaky pixel diff. I looked for unit/integration coverage of the harness: globbed packages/frontend/scripts/** (no test files, no *.test.mjs), grepped the repo for `waitForFontsReady`/`VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES`/`fonts.check` (hits only in the script itself, packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts and docs/task markdown), and checked packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/{ensure-font-link,font-catalog}.test.ts, which cover link-injection URL building, not capture-time font settling.

finding.summary: New `.catch(() => {})` plus `fonts.check()`'s fallback semantics make the font guard pass vacuously when the webfont stylesheet never loads
finding.evidence: The load pass now swallows every rejection (`document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})`, line 374). The comment claims "the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family", and docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-55 repeats that "an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com now reports a clear timeout". verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: verify-visual-browser.mjs:374 swallows every fonts.load() rejection, and the only hard gate is fonts.check() at :388 plus a status !== "loading" poll at :395. Because check() returns true when no matching FontFace is registered, a blocked/failed index.html Google Fonts stylesheet leaves zero Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono faces registered and both polls pass immediately, so the guard cannot fail in the very scenario its comment (:371-373) and docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-55 claim it catches ("a clear timeout"). That is a vacuous gate presented as coverage — in this lens. Two nuances weaken but do not refute it: (a) in the stylesheet-never-loads case load() would not have rejected pre-diff either, so the .catch is not the cause there (it matters only when a registered face's fetch fails); (b) in compare mode the downstream baseline pixel diff (:569-596) would still fail the run, though in UPDATE_VISUAL_BROWSER_BASELINE mode (:533-546) fallback-rendered captures are written into the baselines with no gate at all. No named refutation ground applies, so the finding stands.
